decisions.rationale: Building GameView and DealOrchestrator against unverified glyph shapes and a cardWidth formula risks broad rework across every consuming view if legibility fails at accessibility1 Dynamic Type; the legibility gate has been the pipeline's longest-standing unresolved risk and is cheapest to fail early.
rejected_alternatives: Codex's original ordering placing the full visual system (including card faces) as milestone 6, after gameplay UX in milestone 4
constraints: Task-assignment phase must schedule CardGalleryDebugView's legibility pass to complete before any gameplay UI milestone begins consuming CardView/glyph shapes

decisions.decision: GameState's pile storage is changed from piles: [PileID: [Card]] to a named-field struct (stock, waste, foundations: [Suit: [Card]], tableau: [[Card]]).
decisions.rationale: Swift's synthesized Codable for a non-String/Int-keyed dictionary (PileID has associated values) falls back to encoding as a flat alternating unkeyed array, producing non-inspectable JSON, non-guaranteed iteration order, and forcing RestoreIntegrityService to defensively iterate a dictionary instead of enumerating fixed fields.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving piles as a PileID-keyed dictionary as originally drafted in tech_specs' interfaces-json
constraints: Domain milestone must include a round-trip Codable unit test for this structure before persistence work depends on it
RestoreIntegrityService and all pile-iterating logic must use named fields, not dictionary iteration

decisions.decision: On scenePhase background transition, the app must freeze/finalize elapsedSeconds (stop the timer) strictly before the unconditional persistence flush fires.
decisions.rationale: Two independently-locked decisions (timer pauses on background; unconditional flush on background) were never sequenced relative to each other, creating a race that could persist a slightly-wrong elapsed time — exactly the class of 'app lied about the player's own data' bug this pipeline has repeatedly guarded against.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving the two lifecycle handlers unordered/independent
constraints: Persistence/lifecycle milestone exit gate must implement and test this exact ordering

decisions.decision: Draw-3 stuck-detection verification requires hand-constructed adversarial board fixtures (a board with exactly one legal move buried in a specific stock-cycle position), in addition to randomized fuzzing, before the verification milestone is considered complete.
decisions.rationale: Randomized fuzzing is much more likely to produce obviously-many-legal-moves or obviously-no-cards-left boards than the narrow 'exactly one buried move' case that would actually expose a false-stuck bug in the released 'never falsely reports stuck' promise.
rejected_alternatives: Treating randomized fuzz coverage alone as sufficient proof of the never-falsely-stuck guarantee
constraints: Verification milestone must include a named adversarial fixture test suite for DrawThreeStuckDetector, distinct from the randomized invariant fuzz suite

decisions.decision: The undo-stack-in-GameSaveFile debounce window (~300-500ms) is documented as a floor that must not be lowered without a new decision re-evaluating I/O cost.
decisions.rationale: Each debounced save serializes up to 200 full-state undo snapshots (roughly 100-200KB); naming the floor explicitly prevents a future 'make saves feel snappier' change from reintroducing I/O-induced stutter during the exact spring animations DealOrchestrator exists to protect.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving the debounce window as an unannotated tunable with no documented rationale
constraints: Any change to the debounce interval must be logged as its own decision, not a silent tuning tweak

decisions.decision: Final build plan is locked as 8 sequenced milestones (Scaffolding/CI -> Domain Engine -> Persistence/Recovery -> Card Visual Foundation & Legibility Gate -> Gameplay UX -> Stats/Settings -> Lighting Scenes/Haptics Polish -> Verification & Repair) with explicit exit gates per milestone and an estimated 16-19 engineering days, including a dedicated verification-and-repair milestone rather than end-of-project polish.
decisions.rationale: Combines Codex's milestone breakdown with the systems-risk resequencing and fixes (DEC-project_plan-001 through 005) into one executable plan satisfying the phase's required outputs: milestones, dependencies, risk mitigations, and a verification plan that isn't deferred to the end.
rejected_alternatives: Treating verification as end-of-project polish with no dedicated repair budget
Keeping Codex's original milestone ordering unmodified
constraints: Task-assignment phase must follow this milestone order and dependency chain (Domain -> Persistence (parallel) -> Card Visual Foundation (hard gate) -> Gameplay UX -> Stats/Settings -> Lighting/Haptics -> Verification)
Verification milestone must include the adversarial draw-3 fixtures and the backgrounding-ordering test named in this phase's decisions, not only generic fuzzing

decisions.decision: Project scaffolds as a single Xcode project at SolitaireAtelier/ with one app target, one unit test target, and one UI test target, using exactly the module folder layout already locked in tech_specs — no new structure invented, folders assigned per the owning_lane tags already present in interfaces-json.
decisions.rationale: The working directory is empty (fresh scaffold), so there's no existing structure to reconcile against; operationalizing an already-twice-agreed module layout into literal folder ownership is the cheapest, lowest-risk way to assign work.
rejected_alternatives: Inventing a different folder structure for the build phase
constraints: Build workers must not add top-level folders beyond the locked module list

decisions.decision: The card visual foundation legibility gate (T-021, CardGalleryDebugView) is encoded as an actual blocking depends_on edge in the task graph — every gameplay-UI task that consumes CardView/glyph shapes (T-022 onward) depends directly on T-021, not merely on T-020 (CardView) compiling.
decisions.rationale: A milestone-plan sentence saying 'legibility must pass before gameplay UI' is not mechanically enforceable; without a literal dependency edge, a primary_ui worker has no structural reason not to start GameView the moment CardView compiles, regardless of whether the legibility pass has actually happened.
rejected_alternatives: Relying on the milestone plan's prose ordering alone without a graph-level dependency
constraints: A FAIL on T-021's manual legibility pass blocks T-022 onward and reopens T-019/T-020; it cannot be silently skipped by starting downstream work early

decisions.decision: GameEngine.swift and SolitaireAtelierApp.swift are designated integrator-owned, single-task files: GameEngine.swift is data_domain-owned and frozen once its public signature matches interfaces-json (other lanes call its public API only, never edit its body), and SolitaireAtelierApp.swift is edited only via one explicit services_utilities integration task (T-029), never by ad-hoc additions from any lane mid-build.
decisions.rationale: These are the only two files multiple lanes would otherwise have a real reason to touch simultaneously (DI wiring, scenePhase handling, environment injection); treating them as shared-edit surface risks race conditions and silent structural drift, whereas naming them as single-task-owned turns a coordination problem into a scheduling one.
rejected_alternatives: Allowing any lane to add to these files as needed during their own tasks
constraints: Any change to GameEngine's public signature or to SolitaireAtelierApp.swift outside its designated task is a stop-the-line event, not a silent edit

decisions.decision: Branch/merge strategy is one branch per lane (lane/data-domain, lane/primary-ui, lane/services-utilities, lane/polish-resilience) cut from main after T-000 lands directly on main; each lane merges back at its own milestone exit gate, not continuously, and no lane may merge past the legibility gate until it is verified, not just apparently complete.
decisions.rationale: This matches the already-locked 8-milestone exit-gate structure from project_plan and avoids partially-working intermediate states on main, while keeping the four lanes' work genuinely parallelizable after the shared scaffolding task unblocks everyone.
rejected_alternatives: Continuous small merges to main from all lanes without gate checkpoints
constraints: Merges to main must correspond to a milestone exit gate being satisfied, not just a task being marked done

decisions.decision: Testing responsibility follows ownership: each lane owns unit tests for its own types (data_domain owns the fuzz/invariant suite and adversarial draw-3 fixtures; services_utilities owns corrupt-save and backgrounding-ordering tests; primary_ui owns DealOrchestrator plan tests), while XCUITest flows, the accessibility audit, and layout-overlap checks belong to polish_resilience specifically because it is the one lane touching every screen at once.
decisions.rationale: Keeping test ownership aligned with implementation ownership avoids a lane writing tests against another lane's internals it doesn't fully understand, while cross-cutting integration bugs are best caught by the lane whose whole job is looking across all screens simultaneously.
rejected_alternatives: Centralizing all testing in one lane regardless of who implemented the underlying code
constraints: Every task's acceptance criteria specify which test suite proves it, tied to the owning lane

decisions.decision: Frozen cross-lane types from interfaces-json (Card, PileID, GameState, MoveOutcome, InteractionState, etc.) may not be renegotiated mid-build by any single lane; a genuinely needed signature change is a stop-the-line event requiring explicit cross-lane communication, not a silent workaround in one lane's branch.
decisions.rationale: Since tech_specs' interfaces-json is the canonical cross-lane type contract, a silent unilateral change would break any other lane that already built against the original shape without anyone knowing until integration.
rejected_alternatives: Allowing lanes to adjust shared types locally and reconcile at merge time
constraints: Any interfaces-json type change discovered as necessary during build must be raised explicitly before being implemented, not merged silently

decisions.decision: Two previously-locked flows — resume-in-progress-game-without-replay and corrupt-save-recovery-to-fresh-deal — must be restored into flows-json with concrete state assertions and mapped to explicit XCUITest cases before build proceeds; they had been dropped between task_assignments' draft and its final locked output.
decisions.rationale: design_discussion and detailed_discussion both locked specific, numbered behavior for these exact paths (non-blocking recovery banner, no-replay-on-resume) precisely because they are the least forgiving moments in an app with no menu screen to hide behind; without them in the active flows contract, T-031's XCUITest suite would never mechanically exercise them and a broken recovery banner or a replaying deal-on-resume would only surface during human verification.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving the flows-json as-is with only the 8 flows that survived task_assignments' final pass
Treating this gap as acceptable since the underlying behavior is still described in prose elsewhere
constraints: Resume flow must assert the deal/flip animation does NOT play and tableau/undo-count/elapsed-time match exactly pre-kill
Corrupt-recovery flow must assert the deal/flip DOES play, followed by a dismissible RecoveryBanner appearing only after the deal settles, never before
Both flows need accessibility-identifier hooks consistent with the other eight flows

decisions.decision: Requirement-ID reconciliation against the real, already-produced requirements.json (from app_features) is a fast mechanical diff that runs in parallel with T-000 rather than blocking it, but must complete and be corrected before any task from T-001 onward can be marked done against its acceptance criteria.
decisions.rationale: The requirements.json already exists — app_features finalized a 33-core/2-non-core R-ID file — task_assignments simply didn't have it in context when building the backlog, so this is a mapping task, not a research or audit task; skipping it risks a core requirement having zero task coverage, discoverable only at final verification, which is a far more expensive place to find the gap than now.
rejected_alternatives: Treating reconciliation as fully non-blocking busywork with no real gate (Claude's original round-1 position)
Treating reconciliation as a hard blocker on T-000/build start entirely (Codex's original round-1 position)
constraints: T-000 (pure scaffolding, references zero R-IDs) may start immediately
Every task from T-001 onward must have its requirement_ids corrected against the real file before that task's completion is accepted

decisions.decision: Card-back selection ships with exactly two selectable, visually distinct card backs (the signature Baize & Vellum back plus one clearly different alternate, e.g. a simpler pewter linework pattern) as the locked minimum for this build.
decisions.rationale: The original prompt names 'card back selection' as a feature and CardBackPicker is already a locked component, but no phase across the entire pipeline ever defined what 'the minimum' viable set of backs actually is; shipping exactly one back would make the picker a control with nothing to pick between — a functional placeholder that violates the no-placeholder-screens bar this pipeline enforces everywhere else.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving the minimum undefined and letting a build lane discover/decide it ad hoc
Shipping only one card back since it's the cheapest technically-compliant option
constraints: T-026 (SettingsView + CardBackPicker) acceptance criteria must require exactly two distinct, selectable card backs with visually distinguishable art, not a stub picker

decisions.decision: StatsEvent.gameStarted fires exactly once per genuinely fresh deal — first launch with no valid restore, or an explicit New Game/draw-mode-change confirmation — and never on a resumed cold launch or on the app merely foregrounding an already-active session.
decisions.rationale: tech_specs locked gameStarted as 'written immediately at session start' specifically so an abandoned/crashed session isn't silently lost, but never defined 'session start' against the resume-first launch model; if a cold-launch resume of an in-progress game re-fires gameStarted, every relaunch inflates gamesPlayed, directly violating this app's core promise of never lying about the player's own data.
rejected_alternatives: Firing gameStarted on any app-become-active event
Leaving the exact firing boundary undefined and letting services_utilities interpret it during implementation
constraints: T-008 (GameEngine) and T-013 (StatsLogStore) must implement gameStarted as bound only to fresh-deal entry points, never resume or foreground events

decisions.decision: The card-glyph legibility gate (T-021) requires an auditable screenshot artifact — CardGalleryDebugView rendered at the true on-device cardWidth() output through accessibility1 Dynamic Type, captured as an image with a recorded PASS/FAIL decision tied to it — rather than an unspecified 'manual pass'; a FAIL triggers a pre-approved bounded fallback (flatten only the corner-index/center-pip zone to solid flat ink with a larger index and bolder stroke) instead of an open-ended glyph-system redesign.
decisions.rationale: Five-plus consecutive phases flagged card-glyph legibility at true on-device size as the pipeline's single longest-standing untested risk without ever naming a concrete, unhandwaveable verification mechanism; a recorded screenshot artifact makes this an actual gate rather than a vibe check, and project_plan already admitted the 16-19 day schedule has zero slack for an open-ended redesign if legibility fails, so the fallback must be pre-scoped and cheap.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving legibility verification as an unspecified manual check with no recorded artifact
Requiring a full glyph-system redesign as the only fallback if legibility fails
Mandating an external automated scoring tool as the only acceptable verification method
constraints: T-021 must produce and retain a screenshot artifact of CardGalleryDebugView at true cardWidth() through accessibility1, with a PASS/FAIL recorded against it before T-022 onward may start
A FAIL is resolved only via the named bounded fallback (corner-index/pip zone flattening), not a broader redesign, unless a new decision explicitly reopens this

decisions.decision: The Xcode project/app target is named SolitaireAtelier (matching already-locked Swift file conventions like SolitaireAtelierApp.swift), while the outer working-directory/repo slug remains solitaire-atelier — stated explicitly in T-000's acceptance criteria as a deliberate app-name-vs-repo-slug distinction, not an inconsistency to reconcile.
decisions.rationale: Task paths and file names across task_assignments already assumed SolitaireAtelier/ as the project root without ever stating the relationship to the solitaire-atelier working-directory slug explicitly, risking a lane inventing a third naming variant during scaffolding.
rejected_alternatives: Renaming the Xcode project to match the lowercase-hyphenated repo slug
Leaving the naming relationship unstated and implicit
constraints: T-000 acceptance criteria must state this naming convention explicitly so no lane deviates from it

decisions.decision: The QA checklist opens with a dedicated pre-flight test (QA-000) probing the exact corrupt-save/restore code path that crashed the test suite (AppRestoreCoordinatorTests.swift:54, force-unwrap on an empty/nil [Card]), rather than treating the build's VERIFIED status as evidence that path works.
decisions.rationale: The verification result labeled VERIFIED actually contains an unexecuted test suite due to a crash in exactly the restore/corruption path this pipeline has repeatedly named as the least forgiving moment in the app; a human tester is the only backstop left since no automated run has ever completed this path.
rejected_alternatives: Treating the VERIFIED label as sufficient evidence that restore/recovery works and not calling special attention to it in the checklist
constraints: QA-000 must be run before general gameplay regression and treated as a release blocker if it crashes

decisions.decision: The card-glyph legibility gate gets its own explicit checklist item (QA-004) tested at both default and Accessibility1 Dynamic Type sizes, since no phase across the entire pipeline has ever had this judged by a human or machine with visual access.
decisions.rationale: This has been flagged as the pipeline's single longest-standing open risk since product_research and was never resolved because no build compiled successfully until very recently; this is the first phase where a human can actually look at it.
rejected_alternatives: Treating the gate as already covered by the CardGalleryDebugView existing as source code
Deferring legibility judgment to a future phase
constraints: A FAIL must be recorded explicitly and routes to the pre-approved bounded fallback (flatten corner-index/pip zone), not a full redesign

decisions.decision: Terminal-state testing (win/stuck) is split into three separate checklist items — win, Draw-1 stuck, and Draw-3 stuck — rather than one generic 'test terminal states' item, with Draw-3 specifically testing for false-positive avoidance via a buried-legal-move scenario.
decisions.rationale: Draw-1 and Draw-3 use structurally different stuck-detection algorithms with different risk profiles (exact vs. conservative approximation) per DEC-app_features-002/DEC-tech_specs-009; collapsing them into one test would miss the specific failure mode (false-stuck on Draw-3) this pipeline explicitly guarded against.
rejected_alternatives: A single combined 'test stuck detection' checklist item covering both modes generically
constraints: Any Draw-3 false-stuck sighting during QA is treated as a release blocker per the product brief's own framing

decisions.decision: Multi-card run relocation gets its own dedicated checklist item (QA-013) distinct from single-card tap-to-move tests, requiring a tester to deliberately construct a 3+ card alternating-color run and confirm it moves as one coherent unit.
decisions.rationale: This was named repeatedly across product_research/detailed_discussion as the hardest, most underestimated implementation risk in the interaction model; a tester who only exercises single-card taps could pass QA while this is silently broken.
rejected_alternatives: Assuming run relocation works by extension if single-card tap-to-move works
constraints: Must specifically check for z-order/flicker issues during the group's animated transit

decisions.decision: Stats testing explicitly includes an adversarial data-loss-state test (QA-061, corrupting StatsLog.json directly) alongside the standard fresh-install empty-state test (QA-060), with an explicit requirement that the two must remain visually distinguishable.
decisions.rationale: design_discussion locked these as two structurally distinct visual states specifically because collapsing a real data-loss event into the same '0 games' visual as legitimate never-played status would violate the standing no-fabricated-data rule; this is exactly the kind of requirement that gets quietly simplified under time pressure, so QA must test it adversarially rather than just checking the happy path.
rejected_alternatives: Testing only the fresh-install empty state and assuming the data-loss state matches by code inspection
constraints: Tester must corrupt the actual persisted file, not just imagine the scenario

decisions.decision: The checklist's Known Gaps section explicitly documents that the automated test suite has never successfully executed, the legibility gate had never been visually judged before this phase, and that live drag/win-sharing are intentionally out of scope rather than missing bugs.
decisions.rationale: The phase playbook requires known gaps to be reported honestly rather than silently omitted; a tester or reviewer reading this checklist without this section could mistake intentional scope cuts for bugs, or mistake a compiled-but-unexecuted test suite for genuine automated coverage.
rejected_alternatives: Omitting known gaps and presenting the checklist as if all coverage is complete
constraints: Any future phase reviewing this checklist must not treat 'VERIFIED' compile status as equivalent to 'tests passed'

decisions.decision: The QA-000 corrupt-save/restore test crash and the never-verified card-glyph legibility gate are named as the top two launch blockers, placed above the store-listing content rather than folded into it as caveats, and the app is explicitly not marked launch-ready while either is open.
decisions.rationale: The build's VERIFIED label masks a real test-suite crash in exactly the code path this pipeline has repeatedly called the least forgiving moment in the app, and the legibility gate is a twice-escalated hard release gate that has never actually been checked by anyone with visual access; burying either as a footnote under confident marketing copy would misrepresent readiness.
rejected_alternatives: Writing the store-listing material as an unqualified 'ready to submit' package
Withholding all launch material entirely until the blockers close
constraints: Any future phase or human reviewing this app must treat these two items as release blockers, not polish items
The hero screenshot (mid-game board) must not be finalized as marketing material until the legibility gate records a PASS

decisions.decision: Two additional concrete, previously-unaddressed submission blockers are recorded: no support URL/marketing URL/privacy-policy page exists anywhere in the pipeline, and the actual Info.plist has never been hand-verified clean of stray permission-description keys.
decisions.rationale: App Store Connect submission mechanically requires a support URL (and typically a privacy-policy link even for a zero-data-collection app), and an orphaned boilerplate permission key would be an easy, fully avoidable App Review rejection; neither has been produced or checked by any prior phase in this pipeline.
rejected_alternatives: Assuming Info.plist is clean because the architecture spec says zero permissions were planned
Treating support/privacy-policy URLs as out of scope for an iOS build pipeline
constraints: A minimal static privacy-policy page and a support contact (even a plain mailto: or one-page site) must be stood up before submission
Info.plist must be read and confirmed empty of usage-description keys before submission, not assumed

decisions.decision: App Store positioning leads with the trust/privacy differentiator ('no ads, no tracking, no account') as the primary claim, with the bespoke visual system as the secondary hook, and the App Privacy nutrition label is locked as 'Data Not Collected' across every category.
decisions.rationale: This app's real edge in a saturated, ad-laden freemium-solitaire category is verifiable honesty (zero network calls, zero accounts, zero analytics per the architecture decisions locked since ios_architecture_review), which is rare enough in this category to be a legitimate marketing claim rather than boilerplate; the privacy label is a direct, structural consequence of the locked zero-collection architecture, not a judgment call.
rejected_alternatives: Leading positioning purely on visual/design-award framing without the privacy angle
Leaving the privacy label as an open question pending further review
constraints: The App Store Connect submission-time 'Data Not Collected' toggle must be set manually at submission as its own checklist item, not assumed to follow from this label description

decisions.decision: Subscription/paywall review risk is recorded as a clean pass with no monetization surface at all (zero IAP, zero StoreKit), consistent with the locked no-monetization non-goal, rather than a hedged risk section.
decisions.rationale: DEC-ios_architecture_review-011 and DEC-prompt_contract-010 already lock zero monetization architecturally; writing an extensive hedge-everything risk section here would misrepresent a settled non-issue as an open question.
rejected_alternatives: Writing a generic subscription-risk section as if monetization were in scope
constraints: Any future reintroduction of IAP/subscription must reopen DEC-prompt_contract-010 explicitly before this section's 'clean pass' status still applies

decisions.decision: Screenshot plan is locked at exactly 5 screenshots (mid-game light, mid-game dark, deal/flip frame, win screen, populated Stats screen), explicitly excluding Settings, with the light-mode hero screenshot gated on the legibility PASS.
decisions.rationale: Search-result screenshot real estate is scarce and front-loaded (first two screenshots matter most before a tap); Settings is necessary in-app but not a selling point, and a populated Stats screenshot is chosen deliberately over the honest in-app zero-state to avoid underselling the app in marketing material while keeping the actual in-app zero-state honest per DEC-app_features-004.
rejected_alternatives: Including a Settings screenshot
Using a genuine zero-state Stats screenshot for marketing purposes
constraints: The hero screenshot must not be finalized/published until the card-glyph legibility gate records PASS

decisions.decision: Final verdict is NO-GO for App Store submission today, scoped narrowly to three concrete, already-decided-against blockers (test suite never completing a run, card-glyph legibility gate never recorded, unconfirmed requirement/flow reconciliation) plus two submission-mechanics gaps (support/privacy URL, Info.plist hand-check) — not a broader rework of scope, architecture, or design.
decisions.rationale: Every phase since design_discussion has separately flagged these as hard gates or release blockers; conflating a clean compile with 'done' would misrepresent an app that has never had its test suite finish a run or its single hardest release gate (card-glyph legibility) looked at by anyone with visual access.
rejected_alternatives: Treating the compile-clean VERIFIED result as sufficient for a GO decision
Treating the unresolved items as grounds for reopening product/design/architecture decisions rather than narrow, mechanical fixes
constraints: Any future phase or human must not treat 'compiles' as equivalent to 'tests pass' or 'legibility gate passed'
